tweet.text:
One trap many traders fall into is watching other corners of crypto outperform during stretches when their own niche is quiet, and then taking their eye off the ball to chase it.

It rarely works. If you have real confidence in your ability, your style and your consistency then you know your window will come and you will be ready to seize it. 

There is no need to play games you have 0 edge in just because someone else is winning at them this week.

Vitalik Calls for “EIP-8288 Maximalism” So Ethereum Never Needs Another Precompile
> Vitalik says heavy cryptography should be computed and STARK-proved off-chain, verified through EIP-8288, so Ethereum only sees the result, stays lean, and never needs to add another precompile.
Source:
https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2112032009413439704

tweet.text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see
